title: Shure V15 V — 1 kHz Reference Check
source_report_title: JICO Shure V15 mr - Micro Seiki DQX500 - MA707 - Audio research SP20 - EVO4

harmonic_reliability.quality_note: The right channel's third harmonic changed most during recording. Repeat before changing the cartridge setup.

interpretation.summary: An original Shure V15 V with a new JICO Custom Shop MR stylus gives an encouraging result in this Micro Seiki DQX500 / MA707 / Audio Research SP20 / Audient EVO4 capture: 33.33 RPM (−0.02%), 0.025% DIN-shaped wow and flutter, −0.01 dB channel balance and 27.3 dB average separation. THD measured 0.65% left and 0.49% right. The measurer describes clear, revealing sound before break-in and a surprisingly quiet background; the report calls for a repeat of the right-channel third-harmonic check before setup changes.
interpretation.recommendation: Keep this encouraging baseline and repeat the capture before making further cartridge adjustments, following the report's right-channel H3 reliability note. Record loading, tracking force, alignment, test-record and capture settings for reproducible comparisons. A future comparison with modern stylus profiles is planned.
interpretation.alignment_context: The measurer reports an initial azimuth-related reading of roughly −3.5 dB and says Groove Scope for iPhone helped bring the indication within the app's tolerance. The exact dB quantity and the initial numerical record were not supplied, so this observation is not treated as an azimuth angle, a signal channel-balance result or a quantified before/after comparison. The final report separately records −0.01 dB signal channel balance and 1.70 dB crosstalk balance.
interpretation.distortion_context: During adjustment, the measurer observed a reduction in harmonic distortion, particularly the third harmonic, and felt further refinement remained possible. This is a session observation without a supplied numerical before/after record. The final report warns that the right-channel third harmonic changed most during recording and advises a repeat before changing cartridge setup.
interpretation.listening_context: Michelangelo Canonico describes the sound as clear and revealing even before break-in, with a surprisingly quiet background. He regards a carefully aligned JICO MR stylus on this classic Shure cartridge as a promising combination and plans a comparison with modern stylus profiles. These are listening impressions and plans; this session does not establish superiority over other profiles.

provenance.setup_metadata_source: The report title identifies JICO Shure V15 mr, Micro Seiki DQX500, MA707, Audio research SP20 and EVO4. Its input field is blank. The measurer identifies the cartridge as an original Shure V15 V with a new JICO Custom Shop MR stylus, confirms the Micro Seiki DQX500 and MA707, Audio Research SP20 and Audient EVO4, and supplies the azimuth-adjustment and listening context.
known_limitations: Cartridge and stylus hours, loading, tracking force, alignment, anti-skate, physical azimuth angle, VTA/SRA, test-record identity and track, capture settings, software versions, timezone and repeat count were not supplied.
The PDF input field is blank; Audient EVO4 is the interface identity supplied by the measurer, not a recorded input-field label.

The initial roughly −3.5 dB azimuth-related reading has an unspecified quantity and no supplied initial numerical record. It is distinct from the final report's signal channel balance and crosstalk balance.
The reported decrease in distortion during adjustment and the listening impressions are measurer observations; no numerical before/after series or controlled stylus comparison was supplied.
The right-channel third harmonic varied during this recording; repeat before changing cartridge setup, as the source report states.
Reported differences retain source precision and may differ from subtraction of rounded channel values.
The results describe the complete captured playback chain under its recorded conditions; contributions from the stylus, cartridge, tonearm, turntable, test record and electronics were not isolated.
provenance.fingerprint_channel_assignment: L/R assignments follow the explicit L and R labels in the user-supplied filenames; the screenshots themselves do not display channel labels. Both channels show eight rotations. No inter-channel angular alignment is stated in the screenshots.
